listing.name: Ghostship
listing.summary: Native Super Mario 64 port from HarbourMasters.

steps.title: Keep your current Ghostship installation
steps.instruction: If Ghostship already works in Portcove, keep using Play and the management operations available for that installation. Do not replace it or move its data to use this alternative Windows setup. For a separately prepared copy, follow the steps below.

steps.title: Download the official Windows package
steps.instruction: Use HarbourMasters/Ghostship on GitHub and its official 3.0.0 release. Download Nautilus-Alfa-Win64.zip and extract every file into a new folder outside your Portcove library. Keep existing installations and originals in place; do not extract over them.

steps.title: Prepare your own Super Mario 64 files
steps.instruction: Use your own supported Super Mario 64 US .z64 original for the accepted Windows route. The upstream 3.0.0 guide also describes JP input; that is separate from the credited US observation. Keep the original unchanged. Open Ghostship.exe from the extracted folder, select the original in the upstream file picker and let preparation finish. Keep the resulting sm64.o2r beside the game and its other extracted files. Close Ghostship normally before adding it.

steps.title: Add the prepared executable and play
steps.instruction: Open this game’s Files tab, expand Use an existing installation · Installation options, then choose Use an existing installation. Choose game executable and select Ghostship.exe from the prepared folder. Set Start in folder to that same folder and leave launch arguments empty. Review launch details and confirm the registration, then choose Play. Selecting a program records your intent to run it; it does not authenticate a publisher package.

steps.title: Keep updates and recovery with the correct owner
steps.instruction: For this external copy, you and upstream manage updates. Close the game and helpers, preserve the whole working folder including sm64.o2r, saves, mods, screenshots, ghostship.cfg.json and imgui.ini, then prepare a new version separately before changing launch details. Portcove offers launch and registration removal for this copy; it does not offer managed updates, backups, rollback, migration or deletion of its files. Removing the registration leaves the game and data in place. Existing Portcove-managed copies keep their own available management and qualified recovery.

warnings: Do not use an executable-only downgrade from Ghostship 3.0.0 to 2.0.0 with newer save data. Ordinary managed rollback can be held as unsafe; use only the existing qualified, consented recovery route where offered. The external registration does not provide that recovery.
This guide covers Windows. Existing data, source and execution safeguards still apply; a held update or recovery does not by itself prevent an otherwise safe Play.
